newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tietmeyer says regrets ERM II membership optional.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says regrets ERM II membership optional.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said in an interview with afternoon daily Le Monde that he regretted the fact that all European Union countries would not be obliged to join a new exchange rate mechanism to be set up after the launch of monetary union.
The ERM II will limit fluctuations of currencies from countries which do not immediately join monetary union when it is launched in 1999.
"The only thing I regret is that the new system will remain optional and that all European Union member states will not be obliged to take part," he said.
But overall he said he was satisfied with the plans for the ERM II, noting that the future European Central Bank, for example, will be able to initiate discussions on realignments.

"If there were to be a very worrying development on financial markets, the European Central Bank will moreover have the means to bring to a quick end its obligation to intervene, if this were to endanger the stability of the euro," he said.
